description: Run a genetics investigation from primer design through PCR, gel electrophoresis, sequencing, variant calling, functional annotation, and inheritance pattern analysis.

steps.description: Design PCR primers for a target gene region, checking melting temperature, GC content, secondary structure, and specificity.

inputs.name: target-gene
inputs.desc: Gene name or genomic coordinates of the region of interest

inputs.name: reference-sequence
inputs.desc: FASTA sequence or accession number for the reference genome

inputs.name: amplicon-size-range
inputs.desc: Desired product size in base pairs (e.g. 200-500 bp)

outputs.name: primer-pairs
outputs.desc: Forward and reverse primer sequences with Tm, GC%, and predicted amplicon size

outputs.name: specificity-report
outputs.desc: BLAST results confirming primer specificity against the reference genome

outputs.name: secondary-structure-check
outputs.desc: Hairpin, self-dimer, and hetero-dimer scores for each primer pair

process: Retrieve the target region from the reference sequence using coordinates or gene name
Generate candidate primer pairs using thermodynamic criteria (Tm 58-62C, GC 40-60%, length 18-25 nt)
Screen for secondary structures (hairpins, dimers) and discard candidates above threshold
Run in-silico BLAST against the reference to confirm single-target amplification
Rank primer pairs by combined score and return the top three candidates

steps.description: Optimize PCR conditions including annealing temperature, cycle count, MgCl2 concentration, and template input to maximize yield and specificity.

inputs.name: primer-pairs
inputs.desc: Selected primer pair sequences from the design step

inputs.name: template-dna
inputs.desc: Description of template DNA source, concentration, and quality metrics

inputs.name: polymerase-type
inputs.desc: Enzyme type and manufacturer (e.g. Taq, Phusion, Q5)

outputs.name: optimized-protocol
outputs.desc: Final PCR protocol with temperatures, times, cycle count, and reagent volumes

outputs.name: gradient-results
outputs.desc: Annealing temperature gradient results showing optimal temperature

outputs.name: troubleshooting-notes
outputs.desc: Common failure modes and recommended adjustments if bands are weak or nonspecific

process: Calculate theoretical optimal annealing temperature from primer Tm values
Design a gradient PCR experiment spanning +/- 5C around the theoretical optimum
Set up MgCl2 titration at the optimal annealing temperature (1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 mM)
Evaluate band intensity and specificity on a quick agarose check gel
Document the final optimized protocol with all reagent concentrations and cycling parameters

steps.description: Run and document agarose gel electrophoresis to confirm PCR product size and purity before downstream processing.

inputs.name: pcr-product
inputs.desc: Amplified PCR product from the optimization step

inputs.name: expected-size
inputs.desc: Expected amplicon size in base pairs

inputs.name: gel-parameters
inputs.desc: Agarose percentage, buffer type, voltage, and run time

outputs.name: gel-image
outputs.desc: Annotated gel photograph with lane labels, ladder, and size markers

outputs.name: band-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of band size, intensity, and presence of nonspecific products

outputs.name: purification-decision
outputs.desc: Recommendation on whether gel extraction or direct cleanup is appropriate

process: Prepare gel at the specified agarose concentration with ethidium bromide or SYBR Safe
Load PCR products alongside a molecular weight ladder with known size standards
Run electrophoresis at the specified voltage and time, monitoring migration progress
Image the gel under UV or blue light and annotate lanes with sample identifiers
Compare observed band sizes to expected amplicon size and assess purity for next steps

steps.description: Prepare samples for Sanger or next-generation sequencing, submit to a sequencing facility, and retrieve raw data files.

inputs.name: purified-product
inputs.desc: Gel-purified or column-cleaned PCR product with concentration measurement

inputs.name: sequencing-method
inputs.desc: Sanger, Illumina, Nanopore, or other platform selection

inputs.name: coverage-target
inputs.desc: Desired sequencing depth or number of reads

outputs.name: raw-sequence-data
outputs.desc: FASTQ or AB1 files from the sequencing run

outputs.name: quality-scores
outputs.desc: Per-base quality scores and overall run quality metrics

outputs.name: sequence-summary
outputs.desc: Read count, average length, Q30 percentage, and error rate

process: Quantify purified DNA using fluorometric or spectrophotometric measurement
Prepare sequencing library per platform protocol (Sanger: premix with primer; NGS: adapter ligation)
Submit samples to the sequencing facility with required metadata and sample sheet
Download raw data files and verify file integrity with checksums
Generate initial quality metrics using FastQC or equivalent and flag any low-quality runs

steps.description: Align sequencing reads to a reference genome and call genetic variants (SNPs, indels, structural variants) with quality filtering.

inputs.name: raw-sequence-data
inputs.desc: FASTQ files from the sequencing step

inputs.name: reference-sequence
inputs.desc: Reference genome FASTA for read alignment

inputs.name: quality-thresholds
inputs.desc: Minimum mapping quality, base quality, and coverage depth filters

outputs.name: variant-calls
outputs.desc: VCF file of called variants with quality scores and genotype information

outputs.name: alignment-stats
outputs.desc: Mapping rate, coverage depth distribution, and duplicate rate

outputs.name: filtered-variants
outputs.desc: High-confidence variant set after quality filtering

process: Trim adapters and low-quality bases from raw reads using a quality trimmer
Align trimmed reads to the reference genome with BWA-MEM or equivalent aligner
Mark duplicates and recalibrate base quality scores
Call variants using GATK HaplotypeCaller, FreeBayes, or the appropriate caller for the platform
Apply hard or VQSR filtering to produce a high-confidence variant set

steps.description: Annotate called variants with gene location, predicted protein impact, population frequency, and clinical significance.

inputs.name: filtered-variants
inputs.desc: High-confidence VCF from the variant calling step

inputs.name: annotation-databases
inputs.desc: Selected databases for annotation (ClinVar, gnomAD, dbSNP, COSMIC)

inputs.name: transcript-model
inputs.desc: Gene model source (RefSeq or Ensembl) for consequence prediction

outputs.name: annotated-variants
outputs.desc: Variants annotated with gene, consequence, protein change, and population frequency

outputs.name: pathogenicity-scores
outputs.desc: In-silico prediction scores (SIFT, PolyPhen, CADD) for each variant

outputs.name: clinical-hits
outputs.desc: Variants matching known pathogenic or likely pathogenic entries in clinical databases

process: Run VEP, SnpEff, or ANNOVAR to map each variant to its genomic context and predicted consequence
Cross-reference variants against population frequency databases to flag rare alleles
Apply in-silico pathogenicity predictors and aggregate scores
Match variants against ClinVar and disease-specific databases for known clinical significance
Produce a ranked report prioritizing variants by predicted functional impact

steps.description: Analyze variant segregation across family members or a study cohort to determine inheritance patterns and penetrance.

inputs.name: annotated-variants
inputs.desc: Functionally annotated variant list from the annotation step

inputs.name: pedigree-data
inputs.desc: Family structure, affected status, and sample identifiers

inputs.name: phenotype-description
inputs.desc: Clinical or phenotypic description of the trait under investigation

outputs.name: segregation-report
outputs.desc: Variant co-segregation analysis with LOD scores or equivalent

outputs.name: inheritance-model
outputs.desc: Best-fit inheritance model (autosomal dominant, recessive, X-linked, de novo)

outputs.name: candidate-variants
outputs.desc: Final shortlist of candidate causal variants with supporting evidence

process: Map genotypes to pedigree positions and verify Mendelian consistency
Test each candidate variant under dominant, recessive, X-linked, and de novo models
Calculate LOD scores or Bayesian posterior probabilities for co-segregation
Cross-reference segregation results with functional annotation to prioritize candidates
Compile final candidate variant list with inheritance model, evidence strength, and next-step recommendations

description: Conduct a marine biology survey from dive transect planning through species identification, water quality sampling, coral assessment, biodiversity indexing, and ecosystem reporting.

steps.description: Design underwater survey transects with GPS coordinates, depth ranges, habitat types, and dive safety parameters.

inputs.name: study-site
inputs.desc: Geographic coordinates and general description of the survey area

inputs.name: survey-objectives
inputs.desc: Research questions and target organisms or habitats

inputs.name: dive-constraints
inputs.desc: Maximum depth, current conditions, visibility, and diver certification levels

outputs.name: transect-map
outputs.desc: Georeferenced transect layout with waypoints, depths, and habitat zones

outputs.name: dive-plan
outputs.desc: Dive profiles with bottom times, surface intervals, and emergency procedures

outputs.name: sampling-schedule
outputs.desc: Date, time, tide, and weather windows for each planned dive

process: Review bathymetric charts and satellite imagery to identify candidate transect locations
Select transect orientations that cross habitat gradients relevant to the research questions
Calculate dive profiles using no-decompression limits for the planned depths
Schedule dives around tidal cycles and weather windows for optimal visibility
Prepare transect markers, underwater slates, and GPS logging equipment

steps.description: Identify and record marine species encountered along transects using visual ID, photography, and taxonomic keys.

inputs.name: transect-map
inputs.desc: Planned transect layout with habitat zones

inputs.name: target-taxa
inputs.desc: Taxonomic groups of interest (fish, invertebrates, algae, corals)

inputs.name: identification-resources
inputs.desc: Field guides, taxonomic keys, and reference photo libraries

outputs.name: species-list
outputs.desc: Complete species inventory with abundance counts per transect segment

outputs.name: photo-vouchers
outputs.desc: Georeferenced photographs of each identified species for verification

outputs.name: unidentified-specimens
outputs.desc: Specimens or photos requiring expert consultation or molecular ID

process: Swim each transect at constant speed, recording all observed organisms within the survey belt
Photograph each species with a scale reference and habitat context
Assign field identifications using taxonomic keys and note confidence level for each
Collect voucher specimens of uncertain identifications following permit requirements
Compile species counts per transect segment with GPS position and depth

steps.description: Measure and record water quality parameters including temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity, and nutrient concentrations.

inputs.name: sampling-schedule
inputs.desc: Planned sampling locations, depths, and times

inputs.name: instrument-list
inputs.desc: Available sensors and sample collection equipment (CTD, Niskin bottles, probes)

inputs.name: parameter-targets
inputs.desc: Which water quality parameters to measure and at what precision

outputs.name: water-quality-data
outputs.desc: Tabulated measurements with location, depth, time, and instrument calibration status

outputs.name: nutrient-samples
outputs.desc: Preserved water samples labeled for lab analysis of nitrate, phosphate, and chlorophyll

outputs.name: calibration-log
outputs.desc: Pre- and post-measurement calibration records for each instrument

process: Calibrate all field instruments against certified standards before deployment
Deploy CTD or multiparameter sonde at each sampling station through the water column
Collect discrete water samples at target depths using Niskin bottles or equivalent
Preserve nutrient and chlorophyll samples on ice for laboratory analysis
Record all measurements with metadata (time, GPS, depth, sea state, weather conditions)

steps.description: Assess coral colony health using bleaching indices, disease prevalence, tissue condition, and recruitment counts.

inputs.name: transect-map
inputs.desc: Survey transect layout covering reef areas

inputs.name: species-list
inputs.desc: Coral species identified along each transect

inputs.name: baseline-data
inputs.desc: Historical coral cover and health data for the site, if available

outputs.name: bleaching-assessment
outputs.desc: Bleaching severity and extent per colony using a standardized color reference card

outputs.name: disease-prevalence
outputs.desc: Proportion of colonies affected by each disease type per transect

outputs.name: recruitment-counts
outputs.desc: Juvenile coral counts per quadrat indicating reef recovery potential

process: Score each coral colony for bleaching severity using the Coral Watch color chart
Record disease signs (white band, black band, white plague, tissue loss) by colony
Count juvenile coral recruits in fixed quadrats along each transect
Photograph representative healthy, bleached, and diseased colonies with scale bars
Compare current health metrics to baseline data to detect trends

steps.description: Calculate species richness, Shannon diversity, Simpson index, evenness, and beta diversity across survey sites.

inputs.name: species-list
inputs.desc: Species abundance data from all transects

inputs.name: site-metadata
inputs.desc: Habitat type, depth, and environmental conditions per transect

inputs.name: comparison-datasets
inputs.desc: Previous surveys or regional reference data for context

outputs.name: diversity-indices
outputs.desc: Shannon H, Simpson D, Pielou evenness, and species richness per site

outputs.name: beta-diversity
outputs.desc: Bray-Curtis dissimilarity or Jaccard index between sites

outputs.name: rarefaction-curves
outputs.desc: Species accumulation curves showing sampling adequacy

process: Tabulate species abundance matrices by site and habitat
Calculate alpha diversity indices (Shannon, Simpson, richness, evenness) per site
Compute beta diversity metrics (Bray-Curtis, Jaccard) between all site pairs
Generate rarefaction curves to evaluate whether sampling effort was sufficient
Run ordination (NMDS or PCA) to visualize community composition across sites

steps.description: Compile survey results into a structured marine ecosystem report with maps, data tables, statistical summaries, and management recommendations.

inputs.name: diversity-indices
inputs.desc: Calculated biodiversity metrics from all sites

inputs.name: water-quality-data
inputs.desc: Environmental measurements from sampling stations

inputs.name: coral-health-data
inputs.desc: Bleaching, disease, and recruitment assessments

outputs.name: ecosystem-report
outputs.desc: Complete survey report with methods, results, and discussion sections

outputs.name: data-archive
outputs.desc: Formatted datasets ready for repository submission (GBIF, OBIS)

outputs.name: management-brief
outputs.desc: One-page summary of findings and recommended conservation actions

process: Organize all data tables, photographs, and maps into a consistent format
Write methods section describing transect design, sampling protocols, and analytical approaches
Present results with statistical summaries, figures, and spatial maps
Discuss findings in the context of regional trends and known stressors
Draft management recommendations grounded in the survey data

description: Design and execute a social science study: define constructs, build a survey instrument, plan sampling, write interview protocols, code qualitative data, run mixed-methods analysis, and synthesize findings.

steps.description: Define the theoretical constructs under study with operational definitions, measurement indicators, and literature grounding.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The specific question or hypothesis the study addresses

inputs.name: theoretical-framework
inputs.desc: The theory or conceptual model guiding the study

inputs.name: prior-literature
inputs.desc: Key studies and existing measures of the constructs

outputs.name: construct-definitions
outputs.desc: Operational definitions for each construct with measurable indicators

outputs.name: conceptual-model
outputs.desc: Diagram of relationships between constructs and expected directions

outputs.name: measurement-plan
outputs.desc: Mapping of each construct to specific survey items or interview prompts

process: Extract construct definitions from the theoretical framework and prior literature
Write operational definitions that specify observable indicators for each construct
Map relationships between constructs into a conceptual model with directional hypotheses
Identify existing validated scales or measures for each construct
Document gaps where new measurement items need development

steps.description: Design a survey questionnaire with validated scales, demographic items, response formats, skip logic, and pilot testing plan.

inputs.name: construct-definitions
inputs.desc: Operational definitions and measurement plan from construct definition

inputs.name: target-population
inputs.desc: Description of the population to be surveyed

inputs.name: delivery-mode
inputs.desc: Online, paper, phone, or in-person administration method

outputs.name: survey-instrument
outputs.desc: Complete questionnaire with item text, response scales, and skip logic

outputs.name: pilot-plan
outputs.desc: Cognitive interview and pilot test protocol with sample size and criteria

outputs.name: psychometric-targets
outputs.desc: Expected reliability (Cronbach alpha) and validity benchmarks per scale

process: Assemble items from validated scales, adapting wording for the target population
Write new items for constructs without existing measures, balancing positive and negative framing
Organize the instrument with logical flow, attention checks, and skip logic
Design a cognitive interviewing protocol to test item clarity with 5-10 respondents
Plan the pilot study with target sample size for preliminary reliability analysis

steps.description: Design a sampling strategy with target population definition, sampling frame, sample size calculation, and recruitment plan.

inputs.name: target-population
inputs.desc: Population of interest with inclusion and exclusion criteria

inputs.name: study-design
inputs.desc: Cross-sectional, longitudinal, experimental, or quasi-experimental

inputs.name: effect-size-estimate
inputs.desc: Expected effect size from prior literature for power calculation

outputs.name: sampling-plan
outputs.desc: Sampling method (random, stratified, cluster, convenience) with justification

outputs.name: sample-size
outputs.desc: Required sample size with power analysis parameters and assumptions

outputs.name: recruitment-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step recruitment procedure with timeline and contingency plans

process: Define the accessible sampling frame and identify stratification variables
Run power analysis using the expected effect size, alpha level, and desired power
Select the sampling method that balances internal validity with feasibility
Design the recruitment procedure with contact methods, incentives, and consent process
Plan for expected attrition and calculate the inflated sample size needed

steps.description: Write a semi-structured interview protocol with opening, main, and closing sections, probes, and procedural safeguards.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The qualitative research questions the interviews address

inputs.name: construct-definitions
inputs.desc: Constructs and themes to explore in depth

inputs.name: participant-profile
inputs.desc: Description of who will be interviewed and in what setting

outputs.name: interview-guide
outputs.desc: Structured guide with core questions, follow-up probes, and time estimates

outputs.name: consent-script
outputs.desc: Informed consent procedure including recording permission and withdrawal rights

outputs.name: interviewer-notes
outputs.desc: Training notes on rapport, neutrality, and handling sensitive topics

process: Draft opening questions that build rapport and establish the participant's context
Write core questions for each construct, moving from general to specific
Develop follow-up probes for anticipated responses and unexpected directions
Add closing questions that invite participant reflections and final thoughts
Write the consent script and interviewer procedural notes

steps.description: Develop and apply a codebook for qualitative data analysis with deductive codes from theory and inductive codes from the data.

inputs.name: interview-transcripts
inputs.desc: Transcribed interview data ready for analysis

inputs.name: conceptual-model
inputs.desc: Theoretical framework guiding deductive code categories

inputs.name: coding-approach
inputs.desc: Thematic analysis, grounded theory, content analysis, or framework analysis

outputs.name: codebook
outputs.desc: Complete codebook with code names, definitions, inclusion criteria, and examples

outputs.name: coded-data
outputs.desc: Transcripts with applied codes and annotations

outputs.name: inter-rater-reliability
outputs.desc: Cohen kappa or percentage agreement between independent coders

process: Read through all transcripts to gain familiarity before coding
Create initial deductive codes from the conceptual model and research questions
Code a subset of transcripts independently with two coders and calculate agreement
Refine the codebook based on disagreements and emergent inductive codes
Apply the finalized codebook to all transcripts and compile frequency and co-occurrence tables

steps.description: Integrate quantitative survey results and qualitative interview findings using a convergent, explanatory, or exploratory design.

inputs.name: survey-results
inputs.desc: Statistical analysis output from the quantitative component

inputs.name: coded-data
inputs.desc: Themed qualitative findings from the coding step

inputs.name: integration-design
inputs.desc: Convergent, sequential explanatory, or sequential exploratory approach

outputs.name: joint-display
outputs.desc: Side-by-side matrix comparing quantitative and qualitative findings by construct

outputs.name: integration-narrative
outputs.desc: Written analysis of convergence, divergence, and complementarity between data sources

outputs.name: meta-inferences
outputs.desc: Overarching conclusions that neither data source could support alone

process: Organize quantitative results and qualitative themes by shared construct or research question
Build a joint display table showing statistical findings alongside illustrative quotes
Identify areas of convergence where both sources support the same conclusion
Flag divergences where quantitative and qualitative findings conflict and explore explanations
Draw meta-inferences that integrate both data streams into unified findings

steps.description: Synthesize all study findings into a structured report with implications for theory, practice, and future research.

inputs.name: meta-inferences
inputs.desc: Integrated findings from mixed-methods analysis

inputs.name: conceptual-model
inputs.desc: Original theoretical framework for comparison with results

inputs.name: limitations
inputs.desc: Known threats to validity and generalizability

outputs.name: findings-report
outputs.desc: Complete findings section with tables, figures, and narrative interpretation

outputs.name: implications-section
outputs.desc: Practical and theoretical implications of the results

outputs.name: future-research-agenda
outputs.desc: Specific questions and designs for follow-up studies

process: Summarize key findings organized by research question
Compare results to the original conceptual model and note supported and unsupported hypotheses
Discuss findings in the context of prior literature, noting agreements and departures
Articulate practical implications for policy, programs, or professional practice
Identify study limitations and propose specific future research directions

description: Design and run an environmental monitoring program: sensor network layout, data quality assurance, trend analysis, anomaly detection, source attribution, regulatory comparison, and impact reporting.

steps.description: Design a monitoring sensor network with station placement, parameter selection, sampling frequency, and telemetry architecture.

inputs.name: monitoring-objectives
inputs.desc: What pollutants, parameters, or conditions to track and why

inputs.name: site-map
inputs.desc: Geographic extent, land use, and potential source locations

inputs.name: budget-envelope
inputs.desc: Available funding for equipment, installation, and ongoing maintenance

outputs.name: station-layout
outputs.desc: Map of monitoring stations with coordinates, parameters measured, and sampling intervals

outputs.name: equipment-spec
outputs.desc: Sensor models, power requirements, data logger specifications, and telemetry method

outputs.name: maintenance-schedule
outputs.desc: Calibration, cleaning, and replacement intervals for each station

process: Identify monitoring parameters based on regulatory requirements and research objectives
Select station locations to capture spatial gradients, point sources, and background levels
Choose sensor models that meet detection limits and accuracy requirements within budget
Design the data telemetry chain from sensor to central database
Create a maintenance and calibration schedule to ensure continuous data quality

steps.description: Apply QA/QC protocols to environmental monitoring data including range checks, drift correction, gap filling, and flagging.

inputs.name: raw-data
inputs.desc: Incoming sensor data streams with timestamps and station identifiers

inputs.name: calibration-log
inputs.desc: Instrument calibration records and maintenance events

inputs.name: quality-criteria
inputs.desc: Acceptable ranges, drift thresholds, and completeness requirements

outputs.name: qc-dataset
outputs.desc: Cleaned dataset with quality flags on each measurement

outputs.name: completeness-report
outputs.desc: Data recovery rate per station and parameter

outputs.name: drift-corrections
outputs.desc: Applied calibration drift corrections with before/after values

process: Apply automated range checks to flag physically impossible values
Detect and correct instrument drift using calibration records
Identify data gaps and apply approved gap-filling methods where appropriate
Flag suspect values for manual review without removing them from the dataset
Calculate data recovery rates and document all QA/QC actions taken

steps.description: Detect long-term trends in environmental time series using statistical methods appropriate for autocorrelated and seasonal data.

inputs.name: qc-dataset
inputs.desc: Quality-controlled environmental monitoring data

inputs.name: time-range
inputs.desc: Analysis period and temporal resolution (hourly, daily, monthly)

inputs.name: covariates
inputs.desc: Meteorological or other variables that may confound trend detection

outputs.name: trend-results
outputs.desc: Estimated trend magnitudes with confidence intervals and statistical significance

outputs.name: seasonal-patterns
outputs.desc: Decomposed seasonal cycles and their year-to-year variation

outputs.name: change-points
outputs.desc: Detected abrupt shifts in the time series with estimated timing

process: Decompose each time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components
Apply Mann-Kendall or Sen slope estimator for monotonic trend detection
Test for change points using CUSUM or Pettitt test
Adjust for meteorological covariates to isolate anthropogenic signal
Report trend magnitudes per year with 95% confidence intervals

steps.description: Detect unusual pollution events or environmental anomalies that deviate from established baselines and seasonal norms.

inputs.name: qc-dataset
inputs.desc: Quality-controlled data with seasonal patterns characterized

inputs.name: baseline-statistics
inputs.desc: Historical mean, variance, and percentile distributions per parameter

inputs.name: alert-thresholds
inputs.desc: Regulatory or health-based thresholds for immediate notification

outputs.name: anomaly-list
outputs.desc: Detected exceedances and anomalies with timestamps, durations, and magnitudes

outputs.name: alert-notifications
outputs.desc: Triggered alerts for threshold exceedances requiring response

outputs.name: event-characterization
outputs.desc: Duration, peak value, and estimated load for each detected event

process: Calculate rolling statistics and seasonal baselines from the historical record
Compare incoming data against baselines using z-score or percentile methods
Classify deviations as within normal variability, noteworthy, or exceedance
Characterize each anomaly event by start time, peak, duration, and total load
Generate alerts for regulatory threshold exceedances

steps.description: Attribute detected pollution events to likely sources using wind analysis, chemical fingerprinting, and spatial modeling.

inputs.name: anomaly-list
inputs.desc: Detected anomaly events from the detection step

inputs.name: meteorological-data
inputs.desc: Wind speed, direction, mixing height, and precipitation records

inputs.name: source-inventory
inputs.desc: Known emission sources with locations, types, and estimated output rates

outputs.name: source-attribution
outputs.desc: Probable source assignments for each anomaly event with confidence levels

outputs.name: transport-analysis
outputs.desc: Back-trajectory or dispersion modeling results linking event to source area

outputs.name: fingerprint-match
outputs.desc: Chemical ratio or isotope signature comparison against known source profiles

process: Run back-trajectory analysis (HYSPLIT or equivalent) for each anomaly event
Compare chemical ratios at the receptor against known source fingerprints
Cross-reference trajectory results with the source inventory within the footprint area
Assign attribution confidence based on meteorological consistency and chemical match
Document alternative explanations where attribution is uncertain

steps.description: Compare monitoring results against applicable regulatory standards, guidelines, and permit limits to assess compliance status.

inputs.name: qc-dataset
inputs.desc: Quality-controlled monitoring data

inputs.name: regulatory-standards
inputs.desc: Applicable federal, state, and local standards with averaging periods

inputs.name: permit-limits
inputs.desc: Facility-specific permit conditions and reporting requirements

outputs.name: compliance-summary
outputs.desc: Compliance status per parameter and standard with exceedance counts

outputs.name: design-value-calculations
outputs.desc: Regulatory design values (e.g. 98th percentile, 4th-highest daily max)

outputs.name: reporting-forms
outputs.desc: Pre-filled regulatory reporting templates with required statistics

process: Identify all applicable standards and their averaging periods for each measured parameter
Calculate the regulatory form of the statistic for each standard (annual mean, percentile, max, etc.)
Compare calculated values against standard thresholds and flag exceedances
Compute multi-year design values where standards require rolling averages
Prepare regulatory reporting forms with required data completeness documentation

steps.description: Compile monitoring findings, trends, anomalies, and compliance status into an environmental impact report with maps, charts, and recommendations.

inputs.name: trend-results
inputs.desc: Long-term trend analysis from the trend step

inputs.name: source-attribution
inputs.desc: Anomaly source attribution results

inputs.name: compliance-summary
inputs.desc: Regulatory compliance status summary

outputs.name: impact-report
outputs.desc: Complete environmental impact report with executive summary and technical appendices

outputs.name: spatial-maps
outputs.desc: Interpolated concentration maps showing spatial patterns across the monitoring network

outputs.name: action-recommendations
outputs.desc: Prioritized recommendations for source reduction or further investigation

process: Assemble all analytical results into a consistent report framework
Create spatial maps showing pollutant distributions across the monitoring domain
Write the executive summary highlighting key trends, exceedances, and attributions
Present compliance status and discuss implications for continued monitoring
Develop prioritized action recommendations based on health significance and attribution confidence

description: Conduct a forensic science investigation from evidence collection through chain of custody, lab analysis, quality control, statistical weight of evidence, and expert reporting.

steps.description: Document and collect physical evidence at a scene following contamination prevention, packaging standards, and photographic documentation.

inputs.name: scene-description
inputs.desc: Type of scene, size, access conditions, and preliminary observations

inputs.name: evidence-types
inputs.desc: Expected evidence categories (trace, biological, digital, chemical)

inputs.name: collection-team
inputs.desc: Available personnel, equipment, and time constraints

outputs.name: evidence-inventory
outputs.desc: Cataloged list of all collected items with unique identifiers, locations, and descriptions

outputs.name: scene-documentation
outputs.desc: Photographs, sketches, and measurements documenting the scene before and during collection

outputs.name: collection-notes
outputs.desc: Detailed notes on collection method, packaging, and any deviations from protocol

process: Secure the scene perimeter and establish a single entry/exit path
Photograph the scene in overview, mid-range, and close-up before touching anything
Sketch the scene layout with measurements and evidence positions
Collect evidence using appropriate techniques (swabs, tweezers, envelopes) with glove changes between items
Package and label each item with a unique identifier, collector initials, date, and time

steps.description: Maintain an unbroken chain of custody record from scene to lab to court, tracking every transfer, storage condition, and access event.

inputs.name: evidence-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of collected evidence items with unique identifiers

inputs.name: storage-requirements
inputs.desc: Temperature, humidity, and security requirements per evidence type

inputs.name: transfer-schedule
inputs.desc: Planned transfers between scene, lab, storage, and court

outputs.name: custody-log
outputs.desc: Complete chain of custody form for each item with signatures, dates, times, and purposes

outputs.name: storage-record
outputs.desc: Storage location and condition monitoring log for each evidence item

outputs.name: integrity-verification
outputs.desc: Seal checks and tamper-evident packaging status at each transfer point

process: Assign each evidence item to a chain of custody form at the moment of collection
Record every transfer with releasing and receiving signatures, date, time, and purpose
Verify tamper-evident seals at each transfer and document seal condition
Log storage conditions (temperature, humidity, access logs) for sensitive evidence
Audit the complete chain before lab analysis and again before court presentation

steps.description: Perform laboratory analysis on forensic evidence covering trace, biological (DNA), toxicological, and chemical examinations.

inputs.name: evidence-inventory
inputs.desc: Items submitted for laboratory analysis with requested examinations

inputs.name: custody-log
inputs.desc: Verified chain of custody documentation

inputs.name: analysis-priority
inputs.desc: Examination priority order based on case needs and evidence perishability

outputs.name: lab-results
outputs.desc: Analytical findings per evidence item with method, instrument, and analyst identification

outputs.name: raw-data
outputs.desc: Chromatograms, electropherograms, spectra, and images supporting each finding

outputs.name: method-documentation
outputs.desc: Standard operating procedure references and any deviations for each analysis

process: Receive evidence, verify chain of custody, and log items into the laboratory information system
Perform requested examinations following validated SOPs for each discipline
Run positive and negative controls alongside case samples for each analytical batch
Document all observations, measurements, and instrument readings in the case file
Review raw data against acceptance criteria before reporting results

steps.description: Apply quality control checks to forensic lab results including blank monitoring, proficiency testing, measurement uncertainty, and peer review.

inputs.name: lab-results
inputs.desc: Preliminary analytical results from the lab step

inputs.name: control-data
inputs.desc: Positive control, negative control, and calibration verification results

inputs.name: accreditation-requirements
inputs.desc: ISO 17025 or equivalent accreditation quality criteria

outputs.name: qc-assessment
outputs.desc: Pass/fail status for each analytical batch with any corrective actions taken

outputs.name: measurement-uncertainty
outputs.desc: Estimated uncertainty for each quantitative result

outputs.name: peer-review-record
outputs.desc: Independent technical review of analytical conclusions with reviewer signature

process: Evaluate control results against established acceptance criteria
Calculate measurement uncertainty using the lab's validated uncertainty budget
Check for contamination indicators in reagent blanks and negative controls
Submit case file for independent technical and administrative review
Document any corrective actions for out-of-specification results

steps.description: Calculate the statistical significance of forensic findings using likelihood ratios, random match probabilities, or Bayesian frameworks.

inputs.name: lab-results
inputs.desc: Confirmed analytical findings from the QC step

inputs.name: population-databases
inputs.desc: Reference population databases for frequency estimation (DNA, fingerprint, etc.)

inputs.name: case-context
inputs.desc: Prosecution and defense propositions for likelihood ratio formulation

outputs.name: statistical-report
outputs.desc: Calculated random match probability, likelihood ratio, or posterior probability

outputs.name: population-frequency
outputs.desc: Frequency of the observed profile or characteristic in reference populations

outputs.name: verbal-scale
outputs.desc: Verbal expression of evidential weight following reporting guidelines

process: Formulate the prosecution and defense propositions clearly
Calculate the probability of the evidence under each proposition
Compute the likelihood ratio (or equivalent statistic) from the probability pair
Express the result on the agreed verbal scale (e.g., weak, moderate, strong, very strong support)
Document all assumptions, databases used, and sensitivity to alternative formulations

steps.description: Write a forensic expert report suitable for court submission with methods, findings, conclusions, and expert qualifications.

inputs.name: lab-results
inputs.desc: Final analytical results after QC

inputs.name: statistical-report
inputs.desc: Statistical weight of evidence calculations

inputs.name: case-reference
inputs.desc: Case number, requesting authority, and evidence item identifiers

outputs.name: expert-report
outputs.desc: Complete forensic report meeting court admissibility standards

outputs.name: testimony-outline
outputs.desc: Structured outline for expert testimony on the findings

outputs.name: disclosure-package
outputs.desc: All materials required for defense disclosure (data, methods, qualifications)

process: Structure the report following jurisdiction-specific format requirements
Describe methods used in language accessible to non-scientists
Present findings and conclusions with the calculated evidential weight
State the expert's qualifications, training, and experience relevant to the analysis
Prepare the disclosure package including raw data, SOPs, and proficiency test records

description: Design and launch a citizen science project: build a non-expert protocol, create training materials, set up mobile data collection, validate submissions, aggregate results, and communicate findings.

steps.description: Design a field data collection protocol that non-experts can follow accurately, with clear decision trees and visual guides.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The scientific question the citizen data will address

inputs.name: target-observations
inputs.desc: What participants need to observe, measure, or photograph

inputs.name: participant-profile
inputs.desc: Expected skill level, age range, and available equipment

outputs.name: field-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step observation protocol with decision trees and visual aids

outputs.name: data-form
outputs.desc: Standardized data entry form with required fields and allowed values

outputs.name: equipment-list
outputs.desc: Equipment each participant needs, with consumer-grade alternatives for lab instruments

process: Translate the research question into specific observable data points
Write step-by-step instructions at a middle-school reading level
Create visual decision trees for identification or classification tasks
Design the data form with constrained response options to minimize free-text errors
Test the protocol with three non-scientist volunteers and revise based on errors

steps.description: Create training materials including video tutorials, practice exercises, and competency checks for citizen science volunteers.

inputs.name: field-protocol
inputs.desc: The observation protocol volunteers will follow

inputs.name: common-errors
inputs.desc: Errors observed during protocol testing to address in training

inputs.name: delivery-format
inputs.desc: Online self-paced, in-person workshop, or hybrid training model

outputs.name: training-curriculum
outputs.desc: Complete training module sequence with learning objectives per module

outputs.name: practice-exercises
outputs.desc: Hands-on exercises with known correct answers for skill verification

outputs.name: competency-quiz
outputs.desc: Assessment that volunteers must pass before contributing data

process: Break the protocol into teachable modules aligned with each observation step
Create visual examples showing correct and incorrect observations
Design practice exercises using real-world examples with known answers
Build a competency quiz covering common error scenarios from pilot testing
Set the pass threshold for quiz completion before data collection access

steps.description: Set up a mobile data collection app or platform with GPS tagging, photo capture, offline capability, and automatic upload.

inputs.name: data-form
inputs.desc: Standardized data entry form from the protocol step

inputs.name: platform-choice
inputs.desc: Selected platform (iNaturalist, ODK, Survey123, custom app)

inputs.name: offline-requirements
inputs.desc: Whether data entry must work without cell service

outputs.name: configured-app
outputs.desc: Ready-to-deploy mobile data collection form with all fields and validation rules

outputs.name: user-guide
outputs.desc: Screenshot-annotated guide for downloading, logging in, and submitting observations

outputs.name: data-pipeline
outputs.desc: Automatic sync and storage architecture from phone to central database

process: Translate the data form into the selected platform's form builder
Configure GPS auto-capture, timestamp, and photo attachment fields
Set up field validation rules (required fields, numeric ranges, picklist constraints)
Enable offline data entry with automatic upload when connectivity returns
Write the user guide with annotated screenshots for each step

steps.description: Validate citizen science submissions using automated checks, expert review, and consensus algorithms to flag and correct errors.

inputs.name: submitted-data
inputs.desc: Raw observations from citizen scientists

inputs.name: expert-panel
inputs.desc: Available experts for review of uncertain identifications

inputs.name: validation-rules
inputs.desc: Automated checks (GPS in study area, photo present, values in range)

outputs.name: validated-dataset
outputs.desc: Submissions that passed validation with confidence scores

outputs.name: flagged-records
outputs.desc: Submissions needing expert review or re-observation

outputs.name: volunteer-feedback
outputs.desc: Per-volunteer accuracy scores and personalized improvement tips

process: Run automated validation rules on all incoming submissions
Route records that pass automated checks through community consensus (multiple IDs)
Escalate records without consensus to the expert review panel
Score each volunteer's accuracy rate based on agreement with validated records
Send personalized feedback to volunteers with common errors and tips

steps.description: Aggregate validated citizen science data into analysis-ready datasets with spatial and temporal summaries.

inputs.name: validated-dataset
inputs.desc: Quality-controlled citizen science observations

inputs.name: spatial-grid
inputs.desc: Grid cells, administrative boundaries, or habitat polygons for spatial aggregation

inputs.name: temporal-bins
inputs.desc: Time intervals for aggregation (daily, weekly, seasonal, annual)

outputs.name: aggregated-data
outputs.desc: Spatially and temporally binned summary statistics

outputs.name: effort-correction
outputs.desc: Observation counts normalized by sampling effort per grid cell and time period

outputs.name: metadata-record
outputs.desc: Dataset documentation following metadata standards (EML, Dublin Core)

process: Assign each observation to its spatial grid cell and temporal bin
Calculate summary statistics (count, mean, proportion) per cell per time period
Estimate and correct for sampling effort bias across the study domain
Flag cells with insufficient observations for reliable estimates
Generate metadata documentation for the aggregated dataset

steps.description: Communicate citizen science results back to volunteers and the public with accessible summaries, interactive maps, and acknowledgments.

inputs.name: aggregated-data
inputs.desc: Analysis results from the aggregation step

inputs.name: volunteer-list
inputs.desc: Participating volunteers with contribution counts

inputs.name: audience-targets
inputs.desc: Volunteers, general public, policymakers, or scientific community

outputs.name: public-summary
outputs.desc: Plain-language summary of key findings with visualizations

outputs.name: interactive-map
outputs.desc: Web map showing observations and results that volunteers can explore

outputs.name: acknowledgment-list
outputs.desc: Contributor acknowledgments formatted for publication and website display

process: Write a plain-language summary aimed at the volunteer reading level
Create visualizations (maps, charts, infographics) showing major findings
Build or update the project website and interactive map with current results
Send personalized thank-you messages to volunteers with their individual contribution stats
Prepare contributor acknowledgment lists for publications and reports

description: Replicate a published scientific study: extract the original protocol, critique the methodology, design the replication with pre-registration, collect data, compare effect sizes, and write the replication report.

steps.description: Extract the complete experimental protocol from a published paper, noting any ambiguities, missing details, or unreported decisions.

inputs.name: target-paper
inputs.desc: Citation and full text of the study to be replicated

inputs.name: supplementary-materials
inputs.desc: Any supplementary files, data, or code from the original study

inputs.name: author-contact
inputs.desc: Correspondence with original authors if clarifications are needed

outputs.name: extracted-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step protocol as described in the paper with section references

outputs.name: ambiguity-log
outputs.desc: List of unclear or missing procedural details that require decisions

outputs.name: materials-list
outputs.desc: All materials, instruments, software, and stimuli used in the original study

process: Read the methods section line by line and extract each procedural step
Cross-reference with supplementary materials for additional procedural detail
Document every point where the methods description is ambiguous or incomplete
Contact original authors to resolve critical ambiguities if possible
Compile the complete materials and equipment list with model numbers and versions

steps.description: Critically evaluate the original study's methodology for threats to internal and external validity, statistical issues, and potential confounds.

inputs.name: extracted-protocol
inputs.desc: Complete protocol extracted from the original paper

inputs.name: target-paper
inputs.desc: Full text including results and discussion

inputs.name: related-replications
inputs.desc: Any prior replication attempts or commentaries on this study

outputs.name: validity-assessment
outputs.desc: Identified threats to internal and external validity

outputs.name: statistical-critique
outputs.desc: Assessment of sample size, effect size, analytical choices, and p-value patterns

outputs.name: replication-risk-factors
outputs.desc: Factors that may make replication succeed or fail (hidden moderators, context dependence)

process: Assess internal validity: randomization, blinding, confound control, attrition
Evaluate statistical practices: sample size justification, multiple comparisons, reporting completeness
Check for signs of flexibility in analysis (many dependent variables, subgroup analyses)
Review prior replications or failures for this finding or similar effects
Identify context-dependent factors that might not transfer to the replication setting

steps.description: Design the replication study with pre-registration, specifying exact procedures, sample size based on original effect, and decision criteria.

inputs.name: extracted-protocol
inputs.desc: Original protocol with ambiguities noted

inputs.name: validity-assessment
inputs.desc: Identified methodological concerns from the critique

inputs.name: replication-type
inputs.desc: Direct (exact), close (minor adaptations), or conceptual replication

outputs.name: replication-protocol
outputs.desc: Complete protocol for the replication with all decisions documented

outputs.name: pre-registration
outputs.desc: Pre-registration document for OSF or equivalent registry

outputs.name: power-analysis
outputs.desc: Sample size calculation using the original effect size with safeguard power

process: Resolve each ambiguity in the original protocol with a documented decision and justification
Calculate required sample size using the original effect size at 95% power (safeguard approach)
Write the pre-registration specifying hypotheses, methods, and analysis plan
Define replication success criteria (significance, effect size within CI, equivalence test)
Submit pre-registration to OSF before any data collection

steps.description: Execute the replication protocol, collecting data according to the pre-registered plan with fidelity checks.

inputs.name: replication-protocol
inputs.desc: Finalized protocol from the design step

inputs.name: materials-list
inputs.desc: All required materials, instruments, and software

inputs.name: participant-pool
inputs.desc: Available participants or samples meeting inclusion criteria

outputs.name: replication-data
outputs.desc: Complete dataset from the replication study

outputs.name: fidelity-log
outputs.desc: Documentation of protocol adherence and any deviations

outputs.name: participant-demographics
outputs.desc: Demographic characteristics of the replication sample for comparison

process: Set up all materials and calibrate instruments following the protocol exactly
Recruit and screen participants according to pre-registered inclusion criteria
Conduct the study following the protocol with a fidelity checklist for each session
Record any deviations from protocol with the reason and time of occurrence
Compile the complete dataset and verify data integrity before analysis

steps.description: Compare the replication effect size to the original using confidence intervals, equivalence tests, and meta-analytic combination.

inputs.name: replication-data
inputs.desc: Data from the replication study

inputs.name: original-results
inputs.desc: Reported effect size, sample size, and test statistics from the original study

inputs.name: pre-registration
inputs.desc: Pre-registered analysis plan and success criteria

outputs.name: replication-results
outputs.desc: Effect size estimate with confidence interval from the replication

outputs.name: comparison-analysis
outputs.desc: Side-by-side comparison, equivalence test, and prediction interval check

outputs.name: meta-analytic-estimate
outputs.desc: Combined effect size from original and replication with heterogeneity assessment

process: Run the pre-registered primary analysis on the replication data
Calculate the replication effect size and its 95% confidence interval
Test whether the replication effect falls within the original's 95% prediction interval
Run a TOST equivalence test to assess whether effects are statistically equivalent
Compute a fixed-effect meta-analytic combination of original and replication

steps.description: Write the replication report following Registered Report or standard format, documenting all outcomes regardless of direction.

inputs.name: comparison-analysis
inputs.desc: Statistical comparison between original and replication

inputs.name: fidelity-log
inputs.desc: Protocol adherence documentation

inputs.name: pre-registration
inputs.desc: The pre-registered plan for comparison to actual analysis

outputs.name: replication-report
outputs.desc: Complete manuscript following replication reporting standards

outputs.name: data-and-code-archive
outputs.desc: Reproducible analysis archive (data, code, environment) for repository deposit

outputs.name: comparison-table
outputs.desc: Summary table comparing original and replication on all key metrics

process: Structure the report following the journal's Registered Report or replication guidelines
Present both original and replication results side by side with all pre-registered analyses
Discuss protocol fidelity, deviations, and their potential impact on results
Address whether the replication supports, partially supports, or fails to support the original
Prepare the data and code archive for open repository deposit

description: Write a research grant application: draft specific aims, frame significance, develop research strategy with preliminary data, build the timeline, justify the budget, prepare biosketches, and complete the submission checklist.

steps.description: Draft the specific aims page with a compelling opening, knowledge gap statement, central hypothesis, and numbered aims with expected outcomes.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The overarching question the proposed research addresses

inputs.name: preliminary-data
inputs.desc: Key preliminary results that support feasibility

inputs.name: funding-mechanism
inputs.desc: Grant type (R01, R21, NSF CAREER, etc.) with page and format requirements

outputs.name: specific-aims-draft
outputs.desc: One-page specific aims with opening paragraph, gap, hypothesis, and 2-3 aims

outputs.name: aim-milestones
outputs.desc: Measurable milestones and expected outcomes for each aim

outputs.name: significance-hook
outputs.desc: The core significance statement connecting the work to a broader impact

process: Write an opening paragraph establishing the importance of the research area
State the knowledge gap and what is unknown or unresolved
Present the central hypothesis and the rationale supporting it
Draft 2-3 specific aims with approach summaries and expected outcomes
End with a payoff statement describing the impact if all aims succeed

steps.description: Write the significance and innovation sections showing why the work matters and what is novel about the approach.

inputs.name: specific-aims-draft
inputs.desc: Aims page from the drafting step

inputs.name: literature-review
inputs.desc: Key citations establishing the state of the field

inputs.name: competing-approaches
inputs.desc: Existing approaches and their limitations that the proposal addresses

outputs.name: significance-section
outputs.desc: Written significance section grounded in the literature and health/societal impact

outputs.name: innovation-section
outputs.desc: Innovation section highlighting novel concepts, approaches, or technologies

outputs.name: citation-list
outputs.desc: Organized reference list for the significance and innovation sections

process: Establish the burden or scale of the problem being addressed
Review the current state of knowledge with key supporting citations
Identify the critical barrier or gap that the proposed work fills
Articulate what is innovative about the proposed approach compared to existing methods
Connect the expected outcomes to tangible impact on the field, health, or society

steps.description: Write the research strategy section with detailed methods for each aim, including experimental design, data analysis plans, and contingencies.

inputs.name: specific-aims-draft
inputs.desc: Aims with approach summaries

inputs.name: preliminary-data
inputs.desc: Figures and descriptions of preliminary results

inputs.name: methods-expertise
inputs.desc: Available methods, equipment, and collaborator expertise

outputs.name: research-strategy
outputs.desc: Complete research strategy section with sub-sections per aim

outputs.name: preliminary-data-figures
outputs.desc: Formatted figures with legends showing key preliminary results

outputs.name: rigor-and-reproducibility
outputs.desc: Section addressing scientific rigor, biological variables, and authentication

process: Write the approach for each aim with rationale, methods, expected results, and interpretation
Incorporate preliminary data figures at points where they demonstrate feasibility
Include power analyses and sample size justifications for each experiment
Address potential pitfalls and alternative approaches for each aim
Write the rigor and reproducibility section per funder requirements

steps.description: Build and justify the project budget with personnel effort, equipment, supplies, travel, and indirect costs aligned to the aims.

inputs.name: research-strategy
inputs.desc: Approved research plan with methods and timeline

inputs.name: institutional-rates
inputs.desc: Salary scales, fringe rates, and indirect cost rate agreement

inputs.name: funding-limits
inputs.desc: Maximum budget, cost categories, and funder restrictions

outputs.name: budget-table
outputs.desc: Year-by-year budget with personnel, equipment, supplies, travel, and indirect costs

outputs.name: budget-justification

outputs.name: subcontract-budgets

Itemize equipment needs (over $5K threshold) with vendor quotes
Estimate supplies by aim and year based on experimental plans
Justify travel for conferences, collaborator visits, and field work
Calculate indirect costs using the institutional rate and identify excluded categories

steps.description: Prepare NIH-format or NSF-format biosketches for each investigator with positions, contributions, and synergistic activities.

inputs.name: format-requirements
inputs.desc: Funder-specific biosketch format (NIH, NSF, DOE, etc.)

inputs.name: project-relevance
inputs.desc: How each investigator's expertise connects to the proposed aims

outputs.name: biosketches

outputs.name: contribution-statements

outputs.name: training-record

Select up to five contributions that demonstrate expertise relevant to the proposed work
Write personal statements connecting each investigator's background to their project role
List synergistic activities and broader impacts per funder format
Verify page limits and formatting against the most current funder template

steps.description: Verify all grant components are complete, formatted correctly, and ready for electronic submission.

inputs.name: submission-portal
inputs.desc: eRA Commons, Research.gov, or other electronic submission system

inputs.name: institutional-requirements

process: Verify all required sections are present against the funding opportunity announcement checklist
Check formatting (font, margins, page limits) for every attachment
Confirm all personnel have active accounts in the submission portal
Route through institutional sponsored programs office by the internal deadline
Submit and save the confirmation receipt with the application tracking number

description: Complete a graduate thesis from topic selection through literature gap analysis, methodology design, data collection, results writing, discussion, and defense preparation.

steps.description: Narrow a broad research interest into a specific, feasible thesis topic with a clear research question and scope boundary.

inputs.name: broad-interest
inputs.desc: The general research area or phenomenon of interest

inputs.name: advisor-guidance
inputs.desc: Advisor's suggested directions, constraints, and lab capabilities

inputs.name: degree-requirements
inputs.desc: Scope expectations for masters vs doctoral thesis

outputs.name: thesis-topic
outputs.desc: Specific thesis topic statement with research question

outputs.name: scope-boundary
outputs.desc: Explicit statement of what is included and excluded from the thesis

outputs.name: feasibility-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of data availability, methods access, timeline fit, and advisor expertise

process: List subtopics within the broad area and rate each for novelty, feasibility, and interest
Read 10-15 recent papers in the top candidates to gauge the state of knowledge
Draft candidate research questions and test each for specificity and answerability
Assess feasibility against available time, data, methods, and funding
Discuss the shortlist with the advisor and converge on the final topic

steps.description: Systematically review the literature to identify what is known, where gaps exist, and how the proposed thesis fills a specific gap.

inputs.name: thesis-topic
inputs.desc: Specific topic and research question from the narrowing step

inputs.name: search-databases

inputs.name: inclusion-criteria
inputs.desc: Date range, language, study type, and relevance filters

outputs.name: literature-synthesis

outputs.name: gap-statement

outputs.name: reference-library
outputs.desc: Organized citation database with annotations for each source

process: Develop search strings from the research question keywords and synonyms
Run searches across selected databases and deduplicate results
Screen titles and abstracts against inclusion criteria
Read and annotate included papers, extracting methods, findings, and limitations
Synthesize findings into themes and identify the specific gap the thesis will address

steps.description: Write the methodology chapter specifying research design, data sources, measurement instruments, analytical methods, and ethical considerations.

inputs.name: research-question

inputs.name: gap-statement
inputs.desc: The literature gap being addressed

inputs.name: available-resources
inputs.desc: Lab equipment, datasets, software, and budget available

outputs.name: methodology-chapter

outputs.name: analysis-plan

outputs.name: ethics-application

process: Select and justify the research design (experimental, observational, mixed, etc.)
Describe data sources, sampling strategy, and measurement instruments
Specify the analytical methods with software, parameters, and decision criteria
Address validity threats and how the design mitigates them
Draft the ethics application if required by the institutional review board

steps.description: Execute data collection following the approved methodology, with progress tracking, quality checks, and secure storage.

inputs.name: methodology-chapter
inputs.desc: Approved methods specifying what data to collect and how

inputs.name: ethics-approval
inputs.desc: IRB or ethics approval documentation if applicable

inputs.name: data-management-plan
inputs.desc: Storage, backup, and security plan for collected data

outputs.name: raw-dataset

outputs.name: collection-log

outputs.name: quality-summary
outputs.desc: Data completeness, missing values, and quality check results

process: Set up data collection instruments, databases, and storage following the management plan
Collect data following the approved protocol with regular progress logging
Run quality checks at predetermined intervals to catch problems early
Document any deviations from the protocol with justification
Compile the final dataset with a codebook explaining all variables

steps.description: Analyze the collected data and write the results chapter with tables, figures, and statistical output organized by research question.

inputs.name: raw-dataset
inputs.desc: Clean dataset ready for analysis

inputs.name: analysis-plan
inputs.desc: Pre-specified analytical plan from the methodology chapter

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: Research questions and sub-questions structuring the results

outputs.name: results-chapter
outputs.desc: Complete results chapter with narrative, tables, and figures

outputs.name: statistical-output
outputs.desc: Complete statistical output files for appendix or supplementary materials

outputs.name: analysis-code
outputs.desc: Reproducible analysis scripts with comments

process: Run descriptive statistics and assess distributional assumptions
Execute the pre-specified analyses for each research question in order
Create tables and figures that communicate each finding clearly
Write the results narrative reporting test statistics, effect sizes, and confidence intervals
Document all analysis code for reproducibility

steps.description: Write the discussion and conclusion chapters interpreting results in the context of literature, acknowledging limitations, and proposing future research.

inputs.desc: Completed results from the analysis step

inputs.name: literature-synthesis

inputs.name: gap-statement

outputs.name: limitations-section

outputs.name: conclusion-and-future

Explain unexpected results and generate possible explanations
Discuss implications for theory, practice, or policy
Acknowledge limitations and assess how they affect the conclusions
Propose specific future research questions arising from the findings

steps.description: Prepare for the thesis defense with presentation structure, anticipated questions, practice sessions, and procedural logistics.

inputs.name: defense-format

outputs.name: anticipated-questions

Practice the presentation three times, adjusting for time and clarity
